title: Bloom
opening: Three bars came back to the shop. They all have white streaks.

intro.p: A few weeks after the wedding, three bars come back to the workshop. Each one has white marks on it, and each one looks a little different.

talk: Laila beta, three of the bars came back. People are saying the chocolate has gone off.
Gone off? They are covered in white streaks. Is it mould?
I do not think so. It looks more like a chalky film.
Then it has a name. Dadu called it bloom. I think he wrote down how to tell the kinds apart.
First I need to find out why each one bloomed. Then I can fix it.

lines.text: A white mark on the bar is called bloom. [[torn:…test each bar with your finger and a drop of water…]]
Bloom from tempering can be fixed. [[q:Seed it with good chocolate.]] Melt it, stir in chopped tempered chocolate, then cool and work it.
lines.note: melt 45, seed about a quarter, cool 31

lines.text: Pour into the moulds. Tap the tray to knock the air out.

clues.title: Dadu's bloom card
clues.text: Three kinds, with a test for each. Smears under a warm finger: fat bloom. Vanishes under a drop of water: sugar bloom. Dull and soft and stuck in the mould: never tempered.

clues.title: Dadu's seeding note
clues.text: "Melt it to 45. Stir in chopped tempered chocolate, about a quarter as much. Cool it to 31."

clues.title: The shop fridge
clues.text: A tray of bars sat in here over the wedding week. Rafiq Bhai says the door was left open a few times.

clues.title: The three returned bars
clues.text: Rafiq Bhai wrapped them in paper. Each one is marked with a letter, A, B or C.

clues.title: The return log
clues.text: Where each bar was kept: A sat in a hot shop window, B in the fridge and then the kitchen, C was poured and left to cool on its own.

steps.title: Line 1: why did they bloom?
steps.prompt: For each bar, tap it to run the touch test, then choose the cause.
steps.say: Three bars, three tests. Dadu's card says what each result means.

photos.label: Bar A
photos.testText: You press a warm finger on the streak. It smears, grey and greasy.

photos.label: Bar B
photos.testText: You touch a drop of water to the white film. It dissolves and the film vanishes.

photos.label: Bar C
photos.testText: The surface is dull and soft, and the whole bar is stuck in the mould.

causes.name: Fat bloom
causes.says: Fat bloom: the cocoa butter has come to the surface. It comes from poor tempering or a warm place.

causes.name: Sugar bloom
causes.says: Sugar bloom: moisture dissolved some sugar, and it dried into a gritty white film. A cold fridge, then a humid room can do it.

causes.name: Never tempered
causes.says: Never tempered: the chocolate was never taken through its heat, cool, heat steps, so it never set properly.

params.photoHint: Tap a bar to run the touch test.
params.causeHint: Now choose the cause for this bar.

wrongText.fat-bloom: That bar does not smear. Check the touch test again.
wrongText.sugar-bloom: That film does not vanish under water. Check the touch test again.
wrongText.never-tempered: That bar is not soft and stuck. Check the touch test again.

params.unfilled: Run the test and choose a cause for every bar first.

feedback.correct: Fat bloom, sugar bloom, and one that was never tempered. Three different problems, and each has a different cause.

hints: Dadu's bloom card in the Workshop says what each touch test result means.
Bar A smears, so it is fat bloom. Bar B vanishes under water, so it is sugar bloom. Bar C is dull, soft and stuck, so it was never tempered.

steps.title: Line 2: seed and re-temper
steps.prompt: Set the three numbers for fixing the bars with seeding. Right ones lock in.
steps.say: Dadu's seeding note says how to rescue them. Melt, add a little good chocolate, cool and work.

rows.label: Melt
rows.low: Too cool to melt out the bad crystals. The bloom would come straight back.
rows.high: Too hot. The chocolate would scorch.

rows.label: Seed
rows.low: Too little tempered chocolate to start the good crystals. It will set dull.
rows.high: Far too much seed. It will not melt in, and the chocolate will be thick and lumpy.

rows.label: Cool to
rows.low: Too cold. It thickens before it can set properly.
rows.high: Still too warm. The seeds melt and the good crystals are lost.

feedback.correct: Melted at 45, seeded with a quarter as much good chocolate, cooled to 31. Glossy, with no bloom.

hints: Dadu's seeding note in the Workshop gives all three numbers.
Melt to 45, stir in about a quarter as much chopped tempered chocolate (25 percent), then cool to 31.

steps.title: Last line: mould
steps.prompt: The chocolate is glossy again. Tap the tray six times to knock the air out.
steps.say: Pour, then knock the air out.

feedback.correct: Smooth and glossy. The streaks are gone.

talk: "Shiny again. People will think it is brand new."
Keep it cool and dry, Rafiq Bhai, and out of the sun. And never leave the fridge door open.
Bloom is a funny word for a white streak.
recipe: Smears under a warm finger: fat bloom (poor tempering or a warm place)
Vanishes under water: sugar bloom (moisture, such as a cold fridge then a humid room)
Dull, soft and stuck in the mould: never tempered
Fix with seeding: melt to 45, stir in a quarter as much tempered chocolate, cool to 31
reveal.realFact: In real life, bloom is harmless to eat. It only changes how the chocolate looks and feels, and good tempering and steady storage keep it away.
